turns: Morning Priya. Let's start on level two. How are the steel fixers going with the slab?
They finished the reo yesterday afternoon. The engineer, Tom Nguyen, is booked to inspect at eight tomorrow morning.
Good. I noticed the edge protection on the north side is missing two panels near the hoist.
Yes, I saw that too. Scaffold crew pulled them out to land the formwork. I'll get them back in before lunch today.
Please do. Nobody goes past the hoist until it's fixed. Put a barricade and a sign up now.
Will do. Also the concrete pour for level two is pencilled for Thursday, but the forecast says thirty millimetres of rain.
Then we push it to Friday. Can you call Boral and move the pump booking?
Sure. One more thing, the plumber hasn't finished the penetrations in the bathroom set downs.
That has to be done before the engineer's inspection. Ring Dave from Coastal Plumbing and tell him we need it finished by close of business today.
Okay. And there's a defect in the stair void, the formwork is about fifteen millimetres out of level.
Photograph it and send it to the formwork foreman. I want it corrected before the inspection as well.
Thanks for seeing me, Doctor Carter. I wanted to follow up on the patient support program for our asthma inhaler.
Happy to chat for ten minutes. I've enrolled three patients so far and the feedback has been positive.
That's great to hear. Have any of them had trouble with the device technique?
One elderly patient struggled with the dose counter. Actually, she mentioned she had a bad headache and palpitations after starting it last week.
Thanks for telling me. I'm required to report that to our pharmacovigilance team within one business day. Can I take a few details?
Sure. She's in her seventies, started two weeks ago, and the palpitations settled after three days. I'll send the details through the form.
I'll email you the adverse event form today. Would you like more patient leaflets for the waiting room?
Yes, maybe fifty copies. And I'd like to know if there's a lunch education session about the new asthma guidelines.
There's one on the twelfth of November at the Parramatta clinic. I'll send an invite.
Good. Also, what dose would you recommend for a twelve year old?
I can't advise on off label dosing, but I can arrange for our medical information team to send you the product information.
Hi Grace, quick handover for Ben before I head off.
Thanks Liam. How was the morning?
Pretty good. We went to the shopping centre and Ben paid for his own lunch using his card, which is one of his goals.
That's great progress. Did he manage the bus as well?
Yes, he caught the 610 bus with only one prompt. He got a bit anxious when the bus was late, but he used his breathing exercise.
He had his morning meds at eight. His mum called and said the evening dose of his epilepsy medication has changed, but I haven't seen a new chart yet.
So I shouldn't give the new dose until the chart is updated?
Correct. Please call the coordinator, Michelle, before six tonight to confirm. Also, he had a small fall in the bathroom around eleven. No injury, but I logged it.
Did you write an incident report?
Not yet. Can you remind me tomorrow? I'll do it first thing.
He wants to cook pasta tonight. He's working on his cooking skills, so let him lead with supervision near the stove.
Let's open the infrastructure committee meeting. Apologies from Councillor Brooks. First item is the Smith Street footpath upgrade.
The tender closed last Friday. We received four submissions. The recommended contractor is Greenline Civil at three hundred and eighty thousand dollars.
That's above the budget of three hundred and fifty thousand. Where does the difference come from?
Mostly the drainage works. We could defer the eastern section to next financial year to stay within budget.
I'd prefer we do the full length now. Can we fund the gap from the roads reserve?
Finance says there's about sixty thousand available in the reserve.
Then I'll move that we award the contract to Greenline Civil and fund the gap from the roads reserve. All in favour? That's carried, five to one.
Next item, residents on Hill Road have complained about speeding near the primary school.
Twelve since August. We'd like to install temporary speed counters for two weeks.
Agreed. Please report the results back at the December meeting. Anything else?
Just a reminder that the community consultation on the skate park closes on the thirtieth of November.
Thanks for jumping on, Natalie. Last time you mentioned your team loses time on dispatch scheduling.
Yes, we have twenty two technicians and the schedule lives in spreadsheets. We double book at least twice a week.
Our platform syncs with your job system and flags double bookings automatically. What system are you on now?
ServiceM8. And we need it to work offline because some of our sites have no reception.
Offline mode is on the roadmap for the first quarter next year, but it's not available today.
That's a concern. What's the pricing?
It's forty nine dollars per technician per month, billed annually. For twenty two technicians that's about thirteen thousand a year.
Our budget is closer to ten thousand. Is there any flexibility?
I can ask about a discount if you sign before the end of December. I'll come back to you by Friday.
Okay. I'll also need our IT manager, Raj, to review your security documents.
I'll send the security pack and our SOC two report today. Shall we book a demo for Raj next Tuesday at two?
Hi Julie, what brings you in today?
I've had a cough for about three weeks. It's worse at night and I've been a bit short of breath walking up stairs.
Any fever, chest pain or coughing up blood?
No blood. A mild fever in the first week, but none since. No chest pain.
I quit five years ago. I smoked for about twenty years before that.
Okay. Your temperature today is thirty six point eight, oxygen saturation ninety six percent, and I can hear some wheeze on the left side.
I'd like to get a chest x-ray and some blood tests to find out. I'll also give you a trial of a ventolin puffer, two puffs when you're short of breath.
Not at this stage. Let's see the x-ray first. Come back in one week with the results, or sooner if you get chest pain or the breathing gets worse.
Thank you, doctor. I'll book the x-ray this afternoon.
Righto everyone, today's toolbox talk is about working at heights on the roof.
We've got eight on the crew today, plus two from the electrical subbie.
Good. Rule one, harnesses on and clipped to the static line at all times past the edge protection.
One of the lanyards failed inspection this morning. The tag was out of date.
Tag it out and put it in the quarantine bin. Don't use it. I'll order two new lanyards today.
Also the wind is meant to pick up to forty kilometres an hour after lunch.
If gusts go over thirty five, we stop sheet laying and come down. I'll check the gauge at twelve.
What about the heat? It's meant to hit thirty four.
Water breaks every hour, and there's shade at the site shed. Look out for each other for signs of heat stress.
Got it. And the near miss yesterday, the dropped drill?
Yes, a drill fell from the roof onto the walkway. Nobody was hurt, but from today all tools on the roof must be tethered. I'll put it in the incident register.
Everyone needs to sign the attendance sheet before we start.
Hey Mei, handover time. Lunch was busy, we did about two hundred and ten covers.
Nice. How did the kitchen go?
The coolroom temperature was reading seven degrees at two o'clock. The technician is coming tomorrow at nine.
Seven is too high. Did you move the dairy and seafood?
Yes, into the reach-in fridges. Please log the temperature every two hours tonight.
Josh called in sick for tonight, so you're one short on the floor. Emma said she can come in at six.
We're out of the house pinot and low on oat milk. I've ordered both, they arrive Thursday.
And the booking for the birthday party?
Table of fourteen at seven thirty. One guest has a severe peanut allergy, so the kitchen needs to be told.
I'll brief the chef at five. Anything else?
A customer complained about a long wait at lunch. I gave them a voucher for a free dessert.
Hi Mr Kowalczyk, it's Rebecca from Harbourside Realty about your unit at 14 Wattle Crescent, Chatswood.
Yes, hello. Is this about the lease renewal?
It is. The current lease ends on the fifteenth of January 2027. The tenants, Siobhan and Aoife Gallagher, want to renew for twelve months.
They pay six hundred and eighty dollars a week now. Comparable units are renting for seven hundred and twenty. I'd suggest seven hundred and five.
Seven oh five sounds fair. What about the hot water system?
The plumber, Mohammed Al-Rashid, quoted two thousand three hundred and forty dollars including GST to replace it.
Can we get a second quote?
Yes, I'll get one from Hydroflow by the twenty eighth of October. The bond is held with the Rental Bond Board, reference number 4471 9032.
Fine. Please send me the renewal paperwork.
I'll email it by Wednesday the twenty second. Your management fee stays at five point five percent.
